title: Policies for information security
evidence: Information Security Policy v3.1 (board-approved 2026-02); policy portal in Confluence with read-acknowledgement records for all staff.
desc: Maintain a set of information-security policies, approved by management, published to staff, and reviewed at planned intervals.

title: Information security roles and responsibilities
evidence: ISMS roles-and-responsibilities matrix (RACI); job descriptions for Security Lead and DPO; org chart.
desc: Define and allocate information-security responsibilities across the organization.

title: Segregation of duties
evidence: Deploy pipeline requires PR review + separate approver; but in a 25-person eng team several staff hold both developer and production-admin roles.
gap: Residual SoD conflicts: 4 engineers can both author and approve/deploy production change in emergency-access path; no documented compensating review log.
remediation: Formalize SoD conflict matrix; route emergency changes through break-glass approval with mandatory post-hoc review.
desc: Separate conflicting duties and areas of responsibility to reduce the risk of unauthorized or unintentional modification or misuse.

title: Management responsibilities
evidence: Management commitment statement in ISMS manual; quarterly security steering committee minutes.
desc: Require all personnel to apply information security per established policies and procedures.

title: Contact with authorities
evidence: Authority-contact register (state AG breach-notification contact, CISA, local law enforcement, EU lead supervisory authority).
desc: Maintain appropriate contact with relevant authorities.

title: Contact with special interest groups
evidence: Membership records: Cloud Security Alliance, OWASP local chapter, sector ISAC subscription; feeds routed to #sec-intel Slack.
desc: Maintain contact with special interest groups, security forums and professional associations.

title: Threat intelligence
evidence: Consumes CISA KEV and MDR-vendor threat feeds; no documented process to triage, contextualize and action strategic/operational threat intel.
gap: Threat intel is consumed ad hoc; no defined tactical/operational/strategic tiers, ownership, or feedback into risk assessment.
remediation: Stand up a lightweight threat-intel procedure; assign owner; map feeds to KEV-driven patch prioritization.
desc: Collect and analyse information about information-security threats to produce actionable threat intelligence.

title: Information security in project management
evidence: Security review is a checklist item in the product RFC template, but is skipped for smaller projects; no gate enforcing sign-off.
gap: Security requirements not consistently addressed for non-major projects; no evidence of security sign-off on 3 of last 8 launches.
remediation: Make security-impact assessment a mandatory RFC gate with recorded Security Lead sign-off.
desc: Integrate information security into project management.

title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
evidence: CMDB in Vanta + AWS resource tagging policy (owner/data-class tags enforced via SCP); quarterly reconciliation report.
desc: Develop and maintain an inventory of information and associated assets, including owners.

title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
evidence: Acceptable Use Policy v2.0 acknowledged at onboarding and annually.
desc: Identify, document and implement rules for acceptable use of information and assets.

title: Return of assets
evidence: Offboarding checklist in HRIS (BambooHR) with asset-return step; MDM remote-wipe records.
desc: Ensure personnel return organizational assets on termination or change of employment.

title: Classification of information
evidence: 4-tier classification scheme defined (Public/Internal/Confidential/Restricted); applied to key data stores but not to all documents/repos.
gap: Classification not consistently applied to unstructured data (shared drives, wiki); no automated tagging.
remediation: Complete data-classification sweep of shared drives; add classification banner requirement to document templates.
desc: Classify information according to security needs based on confidentiality, integrity, availability and stakeholder requirements.

title: Labelling of information
evidence: No operational labelling mechanism in place.
gap: Labelling procedure not implemented; classified information is not labelled in documents, email, or datasets.
remediation: Define labelling procedure; enable Google Workspace labels / document headers tied to classification tiers.
desc: Develop and implement procedures for information labelling per the classification scheme.

title: Information transfer
evidence: Data-transfer standard (TLS-only, approved channels); customer DPAs and Standard Contractual Clauses for EU transfers.
desc: Apply rules, procedures and agreements for secure information transfer internally and externally.

title: Access control
evidence: Access Control Policy v2.2; role-based access model documented; least-privilege standard.
desc: Establish and implement rules to control physical and logical access based on business and security requirements.

title: Identity management
evidence: Okta as IdP; joiner-mover-leaver automation via SCIM; unique IDs; service accounts inventoried.
desc: Manage the full life cycle of identities.

title: Authentication information
evidence: Password policy (NIST-aligned) enforced in Okta; secrets in AWS Secrets Manager + HashiCorp Vault; no hard-coded credentials (gitleaks in CI).
desc: Control allocation and management of authentication information (passwords, secrets, keys).

title: Access rights
evidence: Provisioning/deprovisioning automated; but periodic access recertification is irregular — last full user-access review was 9 months ago.
gap: No enforced quarterly access review cadence; privileged and third-party access not recertified within policy interval.
remediation: Implement quarterly access-recertification campaigns in Vanta; start with privileged and production access.
desc: Provision, review, modify and remove access rights per the access-control policy.

title: Information security in supplier relationships
evidence: Third-Party Risk Management Policy; vendor security review before onboarding; vendor inventory with tiering.
desc: Define and implement processes to manage security risks from supplier use of the organization's assets.

title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
evidence: Master service agreements include security addendum and DPA; sub-processor list maintained.
desc: Establish and agree relevant security requirements with each supplier.

title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
evidence: Container base images pinned and scanned; but Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) generation is not standardized across services.
gap: No consistent SBOM across all microservices; upstream dependency provenance not verified for all components.
remediation: Generate CycloneDX SBOMs in CI for all services; adopt signed-artifact verification (Sigstore/cosign).
desc: Manage security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain.

title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
evidence: Critical suppliers reviewed at renewal; but annual security re-review is not consistently performed for tier-2 vendors.
gap: Supplier re-assessment cadence not consistently met; SOC 2 reports not collected for all critical sub-processors.
remediation: Automate annual vendor re-review and SOC 2 collection reminders in TPRM tool.
desc: Regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage change in supplier security practice and service delivery.

title: Information security for use of cloud services
evidence: Cloud Security Standard (AWS); CSP shared-responsibility matrix; AWS SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestations on file; exit plan documented.
desc: Establish processes for acquisition, use, management and exit of cloud services per security requirements.

title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
evidence: Incident Response Plan v2.0; severity matrix; on-call rotation; MDR provider runbooks.
desc: Plan and prepare for incident management by defining processes, roles and responsibilities.

title: Assessment and decision on information security events
evidence: Event-triage runbook; severity classification criteria; PagerDuty + security event queue.
desc: Assess information-security events and decide whether to categorize them as incidents.

title: Response to information security incidents
evidence: Incident-specific runbooks (account compromise, data exposure, ransomware); 2 tabletop exercises in 2026 with records.
desc: Respond to incidents per documented procedures.

title: Learning from information security incidents
evidence: Blameless postmortems for SEV1/2; but no periodic trend analysis feeding control improvements.
gap: Postmortem actions tracked per-incident but not aggregated into recurring-theme analysis or control-improvement backlog.
remediation: Add quarterly incident-trend review; link recurring findings to risk register.
desc: Use knowledge from incidents to strengthen controls.

title: Collection of evidence
evidence: No formal digital-evidence / chain-of-custody procedure exists.
gap: No documented forensic evidence-collection or chain-of-custody procedure; risk to legal defensibility of incident evidence.
remediation: Author evidence-handling procedure; pre-stage forensic capture tooling and retention for CloudTrail/EDR data.
desc: Establish procedures for identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of evidence.

title: Information security during disruption
evidence: Business Continuity Plan drafted; security-during-disruption provisions identified but not exercised.
gap: BCP is in draft and unratified; security controls during degraded operation not tested; no defined minimum security baseline for contingency mode.
remediation: Ratify BCP; define contingency security baseline; include in next continuity exercise.
desc: Plan how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.

title: ICT readiness for business continuity
evidence: Multi-AZ architecture and cross-region backups exist; DR runbook written; but no full region-failover test has been executed against RTO/RPO.
gap: RTO (4h) / RPO (1h) defined but never validated by full DR failover test; DR exercise overdue.
remediation: Execute full us-east-1 to us-west-2 failover game-day; document results vs RTO/RPO; remediate gaps.
desc: Plan, implement, maintain and test ICT readiness for business continuity.

title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
evidence: Legal & regulatory register (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, state breach laws, contractual security obligations); reviewed semi-annually.
desc: Identify, document and keep current the legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements relevant to information security.

title: Intellectual property rights
evidence: Open-source usage policy; license scanning (FOSSA) in CI; software asset register.
desc: Implement procedures to protect intellectual property rights.

title: Protection of records
evidence: Records-retention schedule; immutable audit logs (S3 Object Lock); financial/legal record protection.
desc: Protect records from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access and release.

title: Privacy and protection of PII
evidence: Privacy program; RoPA (Records of Processing); DPIA for ETA-prediction model; data-subject-request workflow; privacy notice.
desc: Identify and meet requirements for the preservation of privacy and protection of personal identifiable information.

title: Independent review of information security
evidence: This first-party readiness assessment is the initial independent-style review; no prior independent review and no established cadence.
gap: No established independent-review cadence; prior to this assessment no independent review had been performed.
remediation: Charter annual independent review (internal audit + external assessor at certification); schedule in ISMS calendar.
desc: Review the organization's approach to information security independently at planned intervals.

title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
evidence: Vanta continuously monitors ~80 automated checks; but manual policy-compliance reviews (procedural controls) are not scheduled.
gap: Procedural (non-automatable) policy compliance not periodically reviewed; no internal control self-assessment calendar.
remediation: Establish internal control self-assessment schedule for procedural controls.
desc: Regularly review compliance with the organization's own security policies and standards.

title: Documented operating procedures
evidence: Runbook library in Confluence (deployments, backup/restore, incident, on-call); version-controlled.
desc: Document operating procedures and make them available to personnel who need them.

title: Screening
evidence: Pre-employment background checks (Checkr) for all hires; records retained in HRIS; enhanced checks for privileged roles.
desc: Perform background verification checks on candidates commensurate with business requirements and perceived risks.

title: Terms and conditions of employment
evidence: Employment contracts include security & confidentiality clauses; contractor agreements mirror them.
desc: State personnel and organizational information-security responsibilities in employment agreements.

title: Information security awareness, education and training
evidence: Annual security-awareness training (KnowBe4) with 96% completion; but no role-based secure-development training and phishing simulations are ad hoc.
gap: No role-based training for developers/admins; phishing-simulation program not run on a regular cadence.
remediation: Add annual secure-coding training for engineers; schedule quarterly phishing simulations.
desc: Provide appropriate security awareness, education and training with regular updates.

title: Disciplinary process
evidence: Disciplinary process in employee handbook; referenced in AUP; HR case-handling procedure.
desc: Formalize and communicate a disciplinary process to act against personnel who commit security violations.

title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
evidence: Offboarding procedure revokes access same-day; continuing-confidentiality clause; exit acknowledgement.
desc: Define, enforce and communicate security responsibilities that remain valid after termination or change of employment.

title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
evidence: NDAs signed by employees, contractors and relevant third parties; template reviewed by counsel.
desc: Identify, document and regularly review NDA requirements.

title: Remote working
evidence: Remote-work security standard; company-managed laptops (JAMF/Intune MDM); full-disk encryption; VPN/ZTNA for admin access.
desc: Implement security measures for personnel working remotely.

title: Information security event reporting
evidence: #security-report Slack channel and security@ inbox exist; but no defined SLA, ticketing, or awareness of the reporting path for all staff.
gap: Reporting channels exist but lack an SLA and formal intake/triage workflow; ~30% of staff unaware of the path (survey).
remediation: Publish reporting SLA; route to ticketed intake; reinforce in awareness training.
desc: Provide a mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected security events in a timely manner.

title: Physical security perimeters
evidence: Austin office in access-controlled building; badge perimeter; data-center perimeter inherited from AWS (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestation).
desc: Define and use security perimeters to protect areas that contain information and associated assets.

title: Physical entry
evidence: Badge-access system with logs; visitor sign-in and escort policy; reception control.
desc: Protect secure areas by appropriate entry controls and access points.

title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
evidence: Lockable server/network closet (office switch gear only); restricted rooms; no production data stored on-premises.
desc: Design and implement physical security for offices, rooms and facilities.

title: Physical security monitoring
evidence: Office CCTV at entrances; but no monitored intrusion alarm and camera footage retention is undocumented.
gap: No monitored alarm service; CCTV retention period and review process not documented.
remediation: Contract monitored alarm; document CCTV retention (30 days) and review responsibilities.
desc: Continuously monitor premises for unauthorized physical access.

title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
evidence: Fire detection/suppression and environmental controls in office (landlord); data-center environmental protection inherited from AWS.
desc: Design and implement protection against physical and environmental threats.

title: Working in secure areas
evidence: N/A — Sightline operates no designated high-security processing zones or labs; all production processing occurs in AWS. No on-premises secure area handles Restricted data, so specific secure-area working procedures do not apply. (Applicability reviewed 2026-08; SoA §A.7.6.)
desc: Design and implement security measures for working in secure areas.

title: Clear desk and clear screen
evidence: Clear-screen enforced via MDM auto-lock; clear-desk policy exists but enforcement is inconsistent and unaudited.
gap: Clear-desk compliance not audited; occasional printed shipment manifests left at desks (spot check).
remediation: Quarterly clear-desk walk-through; secure-print + shredding reinforcement.
desc: Define and enforce clear-desk rules for papers and media and clear-screen rules for information-processing facilities.

title: Equipment siting and protection
evidence: Only end-user laptops and office network gear on premises; positioned to reduce risk; servers reside in AWS.
desc: Site and protect equipment securely.

title: Security of assets off-premises
evidence: Laptops MDM-enrolled and encrypted; but no full asset-tracking/geolocation and off-site asset register incomplete.
gap: Off-premises asset register incomplete; no lost-device tracking beyond remote wipe; ~10% of laptops missing last-seen data.
remediation: Reconcile MDM inventory; enable device location/lost-mode; complete off-site asset register.
desc: Protect off-site assets.

title: Storage media
evidence: N/A — Removable storage media are prohibited and USB mass-storage is blocked by MDM policy; all data resides in AWS managed services. No removable media lifecycle to manage. (Applicability reviewed 2026-08; SoA §A.7.10.)
desc: Manage storage media through acquisition, use, transport and disposal per the classification scheme.

title: Supporting utilities
evidence: N/A — No organization-owned information-processing facility. Production supporting utilities (power, cooling, redundancy) are inherited from AWS under the shared-responsibility model (AWS SOC 2 report on file). Office utilities support end-user devices only, not information processing. (Applicability reviewed 2026-08; SoA §A.7.11.)
desc: Protect information-processing facilities from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities.

title: Cabling security
evidence: N/A — No organization-owned data-center cabling. Production network cabling is AWS-managed (inherited). Office structured cabling carries no production or Restricted data. (Applicability reviewed 2026-08; SoA §A.7.12.)
desc: Protect cabling carrying power, data or supporting information services from interception, interference or damage.

title: Equipment maintenance
evidence: Laptop refresh cycle and vendor maintenance for office gear; data-center equipment maintenance inherited from AWS.
desc: Maintain equipment correctly to ensure availability, integrity and confidentiality of information.

title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
evidence: MDM remote-wipe on decommission and disk encryption reduce risk; but no certificates of data destruction retained for disposed laptops.
gap: No documented sanitization verification or certificates of destruction for disposed/returned devices.
remediation: Adopt certified ITAD vendor; retain certificates of destruction; log sanitization in asset register.
desc: Verify equipment containing storage media is sanitized before disposal or re-use.

title: User endpoint devices
evidence: MDM (JAMF/Intune) baseline; full-disk encryption; EDR (CrowdStrike); screen-lock; endpoint compliance gates ZTNA access.
desc: Protect information stored on, processed by or accessible via user endpoint devices.

title: Privileged access rights
evidence: AWS admin via SSO roles with MFA; production access needs approval; but some standing admin access remains and no session recording / JIT for all privileged paths.
gap: Standing privileged access to production for 6 accounts; no just-in-time elevation or privileged-session logging for database break-glass.
remediation: Adopt JIT elevation (AWS IAM Identity Center + approval); remove standing admin; enable session logging.
desc: Restrict and manage allocation and use of privileged access rights.

title: Information access restriction
evidence: Application RBAC; per-tenant row-level isolation enforced and tested; least-privilege data access; deny-by-default.
desc: Restrict access to information and associated assets per the access-control policy.

title: Access to source code
evidence: GitHub with SSO/SAML; branch protection; CODEOWNERS; least-privilege repo roles; no direct main commits.
desc: Appropriately manage read and write access to source code, development tools and software libraries.

title: Secure authentication
evidence: SSO everywhere; phishing-resistant MFA (WebAuthn/FIDO2) for admins; TOTP for users; session controls; brute-force lockout.
desc: Implement secure authentication technologies and procedures based on access restrictions and the access-control policy.

title: Capacity management
evidence: Kubernetes HPA/cluster autoscaling; capacity dashboards; forecasting; alert thresholds on saturation.
desc: Monitor and adjust the use of resources in line with capacity requirements.

title: Protection against malware
evidence: EDR on endpoints; container image scanning (Trivy) blocking on critical; email malware filtering (Google Workspace).
desc: Protect against malware, supported by user awareness.

title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
evidence: Snyk (dependencies), AWS Inspector (hosts/images) and quarterly external scans run; but patch/remediation SLAs are defined yet not consistently met.
gap: Remediation SLA (Critical 7d / High 30d) missed for ~35% of findings; no single tracked vulnerability-remediation backlog with aging.
remediation: Consolidate findings into one backlog with SLA aging; enforce KEV-first prioritization; monthly exec metric.
desc: Obtain information about technical vulnerabilities, evaluate exposure and take appropriate measures.

title: Configuration management
evidence: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) with peer review; hardening baselines (CIS) applied; but drift detection is not enabled across all accounts.
gap: Configuration drift not continuously detected in all AWS accounts; no automated remediation of out-of-baseline resources.
remediation: Enable AWS Config conformance packs + drift alerts across all accounts; auto-remediate high-risk drift.
desc: Establish, document, implement, monitor and review configurations of hardware, software, services and networks.

title: Information deletion
evidence: Retention schedule defined; customer-data deletion on offboarding performed but partly manual; backup expiry automated.
gap: Tenant-offboarding deletion is a manual runbook step; no automated verification that all data stores (incl. logs/derived data) are purged.
remediation: Automate tenant-deletion workflow with completion evidence across all stores; verify against RoPA.
desc: Delete information stored in systems, devices or any other media when no longer required.

title: Data masking
evidence: No masking/pseudonymization in non-production; production copies with real customer PII have been used to seed staging.
gap: Real customer PII present in staging/non-prod without masking — elevated exposure and privacy risk; violates data-minimization intent.
remediation: Implement synthetic/masked data-generation for non-prod; purge existing PII from staging; block prod-to-nonprod data copies.
desc: Use data masking per the access-control and business requirements, taking account of applicable legislation.

title: Data leakage prevention
evidence: No dedicated DLP tooling for email, endpoints or cloud storage.
gap: No DLP coverage for egress channels (email, SaaS, endpoint); reliance on policy only; limited detection of sensitive-data exfiltration.
remediation: Deploy DLP for Google Workspace + endpoints; start with detect-only on Restricted data patterns.
desc: Apply data-leakage-prevention measures to systems, networks and devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.

title: Information backup
evidence: Automated RDS snapshots + PITR; S3 cross-region replication with versioning/Object Lock; monthly restore tests with records.
desc: Maintain and regularly test backup copies of information, software and systems per the backup policy.

title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
evidence: Multi-AZ deployments; stateless services behind load balancers; managed database HA (Multi-AZ RDS).
desc: Implement information-processing facilities with sufficient redundancy to meet availability requirements.

title: Logging
evidence: CloudTrail (all accounts), VPC flow logs, app/audit logs centralized in a SIEM; log integrity via S3 Object Lock; 400-day retention.
desc: Produce, store, protect and analyse logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events.

title: Monitoring activities
evidence: 24/7 MDR monitors infrastructure and endpoint telemetry; but application-layer security monitoring (abuse, authz anomalies) has coverage gaps.
gap: Limited application-layer detections (business-logic abuse, tenant boundary anomalies); alerting tuned mostly to infra/endpoint.
remediation: Add application-layer detections and tenant-isolation anomaly alerts to SIEM; define use-case coverage matrix.
desc: Monitor networks, systems and applications for anomalous behaviour and take appropriate actions to evaluate potential incidents.

title: Clock synchronization
evidence: Amazon Time Sync Service (NTP) across fleet; consistent UTC timestamps in logs verified.
desc: Synchronize clocks of information-processing systems to approved time sources.

title: Use of privileged utility programs
evidence: Admin tooling limited to authorized staff; but no formal inventory or logging of powerful CLI/utility usage on production hosts.
gap: No inventory or dedicated logging of privileged utility usage; reliance on general admin controls.
remediation: Inventory privileged utilities; restrict via allow-listing; log and alert on their use.
desc: Restrict and tightly control the use of utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls.

title: Installation of software on operational systems
evidence: Immutable infrastructure; no manual installs on production; deployments via signed CI artifacts; container image allow-list.
desc: Implement procedures and measures to securely manage software installation on operational systems.

title: Networks security
evidence: VPC with private subnets; security groups (deny-by-default); managed WAF; TLS termination; no public database exposure.
desc: Secure, manage and control networks and network devices to protect information in systems and applications.

title: Security of network services
evidence: Network-service security requirements documented; TLS 1.2+; managed load-balancer/CDN with security SLAs; DDoS protection (Shield).
desc: Identify, implement and monitor security mechanisms, service levels and requirements of network services.

title: Segregation of networks
evidence: Environment and tier segmentation (VPC/subnets, security groups); prod isolated from dev/test; namespace network policies in EKS.
desc: Segregate groups of information services, users and information systems in networks.

title: Web filtering
evidence: N/A — No centralized corporate web gateway/proxy operates. The control objective is met through other controls: endpoint DNS/web protection is delivered by EDR (A.8.1) and server egress is constrained by VPC egress controls (A.8.20). Standalone web filtering is therefore not applicable as a separate control. (Applicability reviewed 2026-08; SoA §A.8.23.)
desc: Manage access to external websites to reduce exposure to malicious content.

title: Use of cryptography
evidence: Cryptography standard (TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest); AWS KMS customer-managed keys with rotation; no deprecated ciphers (config-scanned).
desc: Define and implement rules for effective use of cryptography, including key management.

title: Secure development life cycle
evidence: SDLC uses PR review, CI checks and a security checklist; but a formal, documented secure-SDLC standard with defined security gates is not ratified.
gap: Secure-SDLC practices exist informally; no ratified standard mapping security activities/gates to each SDLC phase.
remediation: Author and ratify Secure SDLC standard; define phase gates (threat modeling, SAST, review).
desc: Establish and apply rules for the secure development of software and systems.

title: Application security requirements
evidence: Security requirements captured in RFC/PRD templates (authz, data-class, logging, privacy); OWASP ASVS-aligned checklist for new features.
desc: Identify, specify and approve information-security requirements when developing or acquiring applications.

title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
evidence: Documented architecture principles (defense-in-depth, least privilege, zero-trust for admin, tenant isolation); architecture review for new services.
desc: Establish, document, maintain and apply principles for engineering secure systems.

title: Secure coding
evidence: Linters, dependency scanning and code review in place; but no documented secure-coding standard and SAST is not enforced as a merge gate.
gap: No formal secure-coding standard; SAST runs advisory-only, not blocking; inconsistent developer secure-coding guidance.
remediation: Adopt secure-coding standard (language-specific); enable SAST as blocking gate for high-severity findings.
desc: Apply secure-coding principles to software development.

title: Security testing in development and acceptance
evidence: Annual third-party penetration test; dependency/container scanning in CI; but DAST is partial and no security acceptance gate before release.
gap: No consistent DAST coverage; no defined security acceptance criteria gating releases; pentest findings remediation not SLA-tracked.
remediation: Add DAST to pre-prod pipeline; define release security-acceptance gate; track pentest findings to closure.
desc: Define and implement security-testing processes in the development life cycle.

title: Outsourced development
evidence: N/A — All software development is performed in-house by employed engineers. Sightline uses no outsourced or contract development houses, so outsourced-development oversight controls do not apply. (Applicability reviewed 2026-08; if outsourcing is later adopted this control will be re-scoped. SoA §A.8.30.)
desc: Direct, monitor and review outsourced system-development activity.

title: Separation of development, test and production environments
evidence: Separate AWS accounts per environment; no shared credentials; promotion via CI only; network isolation between environments.
desc: Separate and secure development, testing and production environments.

title: Change management
evidence: Change management via pull requests + CI/CD with approvals; change log; emergency-change procedure; rollback plans.
desc: Subject changes to information-processing facilities and systems to change-management procedures.

title: Test information
evidence: Test/staging environments have been seeded from production data containing real customer PII without protection.
gap: Production customer PII used as test data in staging without masking or controls — critical privacy and confidentiality exposure.
remediation: Prohibit prod data in test; replace with synthetic/masked datasets; purge existing test PII and add pipeline guardrails.
desc: Appropriately select, protect and manage test information.

title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
evidence: Audit/assessment activities scoped and scheduled with owners; read-only, time-boxed audit accounts; assurance-testing procedure.
desc: Plan and agree audit tests and other assurance activities involving operational systems with management to protect systems.
